Thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick recap and the model shortlist we discussed for your summarization + entity-extraction flows. I focused on options that balance quality, latency, and cost for the 1k token summaries you showed in the call.

Attached: acme-demo-model-shortlist.pdf (shortlist + rationale), redwood-benchmarks-acme-2026.csv (raw numbers).

Key takeaways:
- Primary goal: maintain extractive accuracy on entity fields (high precision) while keeping 95th percentile latency under ~350ms for single-request paths.
- Workload shape: short context + user-provided text (~1k tokens), ~30k requests/day (expected ramp).

Recommended next steps:
1) We provide a 2-week eval with three model candidates and the prompt set attached. We'll run benchmarks against your sample corpus.
2) We’ll run automated quality regressions (prompt-set driven) against your golden examples and flag any regressions.
3) If acceptable, we can set up a canary rollout with automatic fallback to a cheaper variant under load.

Let me know if team wants latency-first or cost-first as the primary constraint — we'll tune the shortlist accordingly.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + next steps (Acme)

Looping in a quick internal note before we send the final reply to Acme.

Based on the workload shape and John's ask, here's my proposed shortlist and rationale (high level):

1) redwood-llama-70b-q4
   - Quality: Best shot at matching current high-precision extraction (top N recall).
   - Latency: ~350-10ms p95 on our dedicated nvidia-a100 (single-threaded), can be lower with batching for throughput windows.
   - Cost: highest CPU/GPU cost; recommend for primary if accuracy is non-negotiable.
2) redwood-mistral-8x (8B)
   - Quality: Very strong on instruction + extraction for short contexts, often within 3-5% of 70b on entity F1 for this vertical.
   - Latency: ~120-180ms p95 (significantly faster).
   - Cost: mid-range; good candidate if latency is primary and slight quality delta acceptable.
3) open-llama-13b-8bit
   - Quality: Good baseline, cheaper; some brittle cases (numeric extraction) may need prompt engineering.
   - Latency: ~180-250ms p95.
   - Cost: lowest; useful for baseline and as fallback during incidents.

Notes on regressions / fallback:
- We'll run the provided prompt set through our eval harness and produce an automatic regression report (precision/recall/F1 + example failures).
- For canary rollouts: automatic rollback on threshold regression (configurable) and instant fallback to the cheaper variant or the previous serving model.
- If Acme wants additional guardrails we can add a secondary validator step (lightweight rules + L0 classifier) before returning results to users.

Action items for reply to customer: include estimated $/1k-token and p95 latency (we should run the quick benchmark using Acme sample prompts). I'll have Dev run the quick perf pass and attach numbers.

—Rishi
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

John / Priya —

Thanks for the prompt samples — helpful. Per Rishi / Dev's note, here's the recommended shortlist with our quick-est perf and cost estimates run against your sample prompts (attached redwood-benchmarks-acme-2026.csv has full output):

Shortlist + quick numbers (p95 latency / est $ per 1k tokens):
- redwood-llama-70b-q4 — 410ms p95 / $12.50 per 1k tokens (best quality)
- redwood-mistral-8x — 150ms p95 / $4.00 per 1k tokens (best latency/price balance)
- open-llama-13b-8bit — 220ms p95 / $1.20 per 1k tokens (cost-effective fallback)

Rationale summary:
- If Acme prioritizes precision on extraction fields (legal/finance-style entities), start with redwood-llama-70b-q4 for the canary eval.
- If 95th percentile latency and cost are tight constraints, start with redwood-mistral-8x and measure delta in the regression report.
- Keep open-llama-13b-8bit as a fallback tier with stricter validator rules.

Quality regression guardrails we propose: 
- Pre-commit evals: run your golden-label prompt set nightly during the eval window and surface delta dashboards.
- Canary policy: start at 1% traffic, ramp to 10% over 48h; automatic rollback if relative F1 drops > 2 points or absolute precision < configurable threshold.
- Human-in-loop: flag the first 500 low-confidence responses to a review queue for 1 week.

Attachments included: acme_demo_promptset_v1.json (prompt set we'll use for evals), acme-demo-model-shortlist.pdf, redwood-benchmarks-acme-2026.csv

Next steps (please pick one):
- Option A: 2-week eval starting Mon 29 Jun — we run benchmarks and provide the regression report + canary plan.
- Option B: Run a targeted latency-first pilot on mistral-8x and evaluate quality delta.

I can schedule a 30-min sync next week to walk through the full regression report. Here's a Calendly link: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30min

If that looks good, I'll open the HubSpot trial deal (ACME-2026-245) and loop in our procurement contacts.
